set_text.text: Inventory carrying cost is what you pay to keep stock you already own. It covers the money tied up in it, the space it fills and the product lost before it sells. It runs as a yearly rate on average inventory: 27% here, or $35,640 a year.
The cost of time on the floor. Every week a case sits, it keeps paying for the money, space and risk behind it.
The cost of running short. A lost sale or a substitution has a price too, so the cheapest stock to hold is not always the least stock.
The $0.50 a case is an average across 72,000 cases. The rate rides on what each case cost, so a case of beef carries far more than a case of napkins held as long.
Who uses an inventory carrying cost calculator

It is built for independent food distributors who hold dated and dry stock in their own warehouse. Anyone who decides how much stock to hold, or signs off on a large buy, should know what holding it costs.
